summary.name: TeXstudio
summary.one_liner: TeXstudio is an open-source integrated writing environment for creating LaTeX documents, with syntax highlighting, an integrated PDF viewer, and reference checking.
use_cases: Writing LaTeX documents with syntax highlighting and autocompletion
Compiling LaTeX with latexmk, bibliography and glossary tools
Checking references, spelling and grammar in LaTeX text
Previewing PDF output alongside source code
summary.what_it_does: TeXstudio is an editor for LaTeX documents that bundles syntax highlighting, code folding, a structure view, and auto completion for commands, references and citations. It offers assistants that generate code for images, tables and formulas, and supports drag-and-drop of images into the editor. Its checks include an interactive spellchecker, grammar checker, and reference checker, with LaTeX errors and warnings shown in the editor and in a list. It has built-in support for various LaTeX compilers, index, bibliography and glossary tools, and Latexmk, and can detect when multiple LaTeX runs are needed. An integrated PDF viewer offers near word-level syncing with the source. The page's release list shows version 4.9.9 as the latest, with 4.9.0 adding collaborative editing via teamtype on macOS and Linux.
notable: Integrated PDF viewer with near word-level syncing and live inline formula preview
Assistants for images, tables, formulas, and drag-and-drop image inclusion
Interactive spellchecker, grammar checker, and reference checker
Collaborative editing via teamtype (macOS and Linux, since 4.9.0)
caveats: Windows 11 requires the Visual Studio runtime to be installed
macOS builds are not notarized; users may need Ctrl+Click > Open to launch
Windows Defender flagged a base library as a false positive in January 2025, requiring an exclusion
No release for macOS 10.x; must be compiled from source or installed via homebrew
